recent_posts.title: Hybrid Preferences: Learning to Route Instances for Human vs. AI Feedback
recent_posts.summary: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) leverage human feedback, which can be costly and error-prone. A new approach combines human and AI annotations to create hybrid preference datasets. This routing framework uses a performance prediction model to allocate preference instances to either human or LM annotators, aiming for high-quality and cost-efficient data. The introduction of MultiPref, a new dataset, enables better performance at reduced human annotation costs and helps understand when human annotations are most beneficial.

recent_posts.title: Ai2 at COP 16: Harnessing AI and Conservation Tech to Protect Our Planet
recent_posts.summary: Ai2 is showcasing its cutting-edge AI and conservation technologies at COP16, a significant event focused on biodiversity loss. Technologies like AI camera traps and computer vision models are transforming conservation efforts by providing real-time data to tackle urgent environmental issues. Ai2's initiatives, including EarthRanger and Skylight, aim to empower global stakeholders to meet ambitious targets for land and ocean protection, emphasizing the need for collaboration and innovative solutions.

recent_posts.title: Investigating Pretraining Dynamics and Stability with OLMo Checkpoints
recent_posts.summary: The post delves into the dynamics of pretraining and its stability by analyzing OLMo 7B 0724 checkpoints. It investigates how parameter and activation magnitudes evolve during pretraining and their impact on stability. The findings highlight that, while parameter and activation norms generally decrease, specific outliers with large magnitudes emerge, which can cause numerical stability issues. These insights emphasize the need for modifying training dynamics to prevent the development of small embeddings and large outlier features for better pretraining stability.

recent_posts.title: Ai2 at DEF CON 32
recent_posts.summary: Ai2 participated in DEF CON 32's AI Village Generative Red Teaming event, deploying their OLMo model to test its security measures. Collaborating with DSRI, they gathered insights from nearly 200 submissions, learning new ways to enhance AI robustness. The experience highlighted the importance of adaptive changes and valuable insights into AI security.

recent_posts.title: OLMoE: An open, small, and state-of-the-art mixture-of-experts model
recent_posts.summary: OLMoE is a new mixture-of-experts model developed by Contextual AI, notable for being open and performant with 1 billion active parameters in a 7 billion total parameter setup. It is on the Pareto frontier of performance and size, trained on 5 trillion tokens and benefits from a mixture of data sources including Ai2’s Dolma and Nvidia’s Daring Anteater. The release includes various checkpoints and fine-tuned versions, plus a new post-training pipeline Tulu 3 for enhanced results in math, code, and instruction-following evaluations.

recent_posts.title: Digital Socrates: Evaluating LLMs through Explanation Critiques
recent_posts.summary: Digital Socrates is a novel tool designed to evaluate the explanation capabilities of large language models (LLMs). It aims to define an in-depth method for characterizing model explanations, create a human-verified dataset, and train an open-source critique model. The tool uses Socratic questioning to identify flaws in explanations and provides both general and specific suggestions for improvement, including a quantitative metric for explanation quality. Digital Socrates’ Critique Bank comprises a rich dataset of model-generated explanations and human annotations. The aim is to provide better insights into model reasoning flaws and improve overall model performance.

recent_posts.title: Open research is the key to unlocking safer AI
recent_posts.summary: AI safety is crucial in ensuring AI benefits humanity while minimizing harm. Ai2 promotes open research to tackle this issue, emphasizing the need to understand model behavior and advocating for community collaboration. They have developed the Ai2 Safety Toolkit to advance LLM safety and foster open science. Key initiatives include red-teaming frameworks, multilingual inclusivity, and continuous safety evaluation throughout the AI development process.

recent_posts.title: Latest and greatest: Ai2’s release notes
recent_posts.summary: Ai2 has rebranded and introduced a new process for releasing regular updates and new assets in its OLMo, Dolma, and associated tools ecosystem. They will share templated release notes on their website, X platform, and via newsletter to keep the community informed.

recent_posts.title: AppWorld: A controllable world of apps and people for benchmarking interactive coding agents
recent_posts.summary: AppWorld introduces a controllable simulated environment for benchmarking interactive coding agents on complex tasks across various day-to-day apps. It includes a high-fidelity API-based simulator, a benchmark of 750 complex tasks, and a robust evaluation framework to determine agent performance. AppWorld addresses the shortcomings of existing benchmarks by providing a rich and reproducible execution environment, and it plans to extend its capabilities further in automating digital tasks.

recent_posts.title: Broadening the Scope of Noncompliance: When and How AI Models Should Not Comply with User Requests
recent_posts.summary: With the increasing integration of AI language models into various applications, ensuring these models can appropriately reject unsafe or harmful queries is crucial. This post introduces a broader perspective on AI noncompliance, outlining when and how models should not comply with user requests beyond just avoiding harmful content. The authors present a taxonomy of noncompliance scenarios and detail the creation of the CoCoNot dataset for training and evaluating AI model noncompliance. The findings indicate varying compliance levels among different models and suggest fine-tuning methods like LoRA can improve noncompliance without compromising general capabilities.

top_posts.title: Elaine Zhong Awarded the 2024 Allen AI Outstanding Engineer Scholarship
top_posts.summary: Elaine Zhong, a sophomore at the UW Allen School, has been awarded the 2024 Allen AI Outstanding Engineer Scholarship. The scholarship aims to encourage underrepresented groups in computer science and engineering and provides full tuition, fees, and textbooks for one academic year, along with mentorship and a paid summer internship at the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence.

top_posts.title: Data-driven Discovery with Large Generative Models
top_posts.summary: Researchers can leverage AI to tackle the challenge of sorting through an overwhelming number of research articles. Large generative models have the potential to accelerate scientific discovery by uncovering complex insights and generating novel hypotheses. DataVoyager, a proof-of-concept system, is capable of data understanding, hypothesis generation, multi-step planning, and interdisciplinary knowledge integration, but it also has limitations in data transformation, scalability, and hypothesis verification. Integrating robust tools and user-centric interventions is crucial for successful data-driven discovery.

top_posts.title: The AI2 Safety Toolkit: Datasets and Models for Safe and Responsible LLMs Development
top_posts.summary: The AI2 Safety Toolkit aims to enhance the safety of large language models (LLMs). It introduces two major components: WildTeaming, an automatic red-teaming framework for identifying and mitigating harmful behavior, and WildGuard, a multi-purpose moderation tool for assessing the safety of user-LLM interactions. WildTeaming creates a dataset called WildJailbreak from in-the-wild interactions to train safer models, while WildGuard provides a comprehensive dataset, WildGuardMix, to improve content moderation by detecting harmful prompts, responses, and refusal accuracy. Both components outperform previous benchmarks and are available for the community to enhance LLM safety.
